newsitem.title: USA: Herman wins battle for Clinton Labor cabinet post.
newsitem.headline: Herman wins battle for Clinton Labor cabinet post.

text.p: Alexis Herman, a White House official who was strongly backed by African American and women's groups seems likely to emerge as the only black woman in President Bill Clinton's new cabinet.
Herman, 49, was nominated to the post of Labour Secretary on Friday after a tough battle among three powerful interest groups within the Democratic Party.
While labour unions pushed hard for former Pennsylvania Sen. Harris Wofford to get the job, Hispanics lobbied for Representative Estaban Torres of California.

But Herman, who had served as director of the White House public liason office since 1993, was strongly backed by the National Organisation For Women, and civil rights leader Jesse Jackson personally lobbied on her behalf.

Born in Mobile, Alabama, Herman is a graduate of Xavier University and began her career in 1969 as a social worker for Catholic Charities. That led to her service in a black women's employment programme in Atlanta and her appointment in 1977 as national director of the National Minority Women's Employment Programme.

She worked in the Labour Department from 1977-81 as head of the women's bureau where she was the youngest person ever to hold that position and the first bureau head to be elevated to the rank of deputy undersecretary.

Meanwhile Herman was also active in Democratic Party politics. She worked closely with the late Ron Brown at the Democratic National Committee where she was a deputy chair from 1989-91. In 1991 she was named chief executive officer of the 1992 Democratic Convention and she worked on Clinton's 1992 transition team.

Despite her experience in employment issues, Herman was seen by some in organised labour as being too close to big business. One of her jobs as head of public liason was to escort groups of women entrepreneurs on foreign trade trips.

Herman can expect some bipartisan support when her name goes to the Senate for confirmation. Representative Sonny Callahan, a Republican from her home state of Alabama, said Herman would be a valuable addition to Clinton's cabinet.
"Her credentials are truly outstanding," he said.
Herman is single and has no children.
